purpose: The fixed top bar: brand mark, burger + Menu word, theme toggle, live scroll-progress readout, sign-in glyph and the primary CTA. Rendered unconditionally on EVERY route.

themeToggle.note: INVERTED: the real markup ships ariaPressed true and dataThemeState "dark" while the page renders LIGHT. Do not normalise.

progressInitial.note: Measured: "0%" (1 token). public/motion/m12.js overwrites it every animation frame.

evidence.structure: Structure, layout and motion measured against the live original. A pixel audit verified 1382/1382 elements at a 1440px viewport and 962/962 at 390px with zero deltas. Copy is the original's own.

constraints.verification: src/layout/Layout.jsx:41 renders <Header /> unconditionally. Checked against all 5 real templates: present exactly once in every one, and it is the first node inside the section.page shell.

motion.detail: public/motion/m15.js reveals .header over 0.2s power2.out; m20.js rotates the two .header__menu-line elements +/-45 degrees over 0.25s power2.out; m12.js updates #progress on requestAnimationFrame; m10.js binds the theme toggle.
motion.reducedMotionFallback: Render the header at its final position with no reveal, show the burger in its resting cross-free state, and keep the progress readout updating (it is information, not decoration).
motion.reducedMotionFallbackKind: design-rule (the source ships NO prefers-reduced-motion handling for this section, so the fallback is prescribed by this repository, not mirrored)

responsive.base: three groups (left / main / right) at z-index 999
responsive.max-991px: no documented change in the stylesheet
responsive.max-767px: no documented change in the stylesheet

notes: #progress LIVES HERE, not in the footer. That means the scroll-progress readout IS present on the 404, even though the 404 has no footer. Only #dotsField (chrome.footer) is genuinely absent from the 404. This corrects a claim in the build groundwork.
contentMaxWordsTotalNote: Set BETWEEN the measured real total and the maximum the per-field budgets allow, so the cap can actually reject an over-long instance instead of being unreachable. extraction/verify_all.py check [p] fails if any declared contentMaxWordsTotal becomes vacuous (>= the per-field maximum). Previously 15, which was unreachable.
